## OpenAI launches two Daybreak security products

OpenAI has launched two new security products, one for penetration testing and one for defense. Both are part of its Daybreak security platform and were presented at a keynote on 12 November 2026, as The Register reported that evening.

OpenAI President Greg Brockman used the keynote for a sweeping claim: "We're now at a point where companies will be secure only to the extent of the frontier model that they use to defend themselves and how well they utilize that." He conceded that security "fundamentals are important, and not to be discounted," but said companies need to "really reorient your security practice around what these models can do."

## Red Team attacks, Defense Factory repairs

Daybreak Red Team is available in early access. It uses OpenAI models to test a company's web applications for vulnerabilities, with a fleet of agents that draws on source code and app context to investigate and test attack paths. Nancy Wang, who leads cyber-applied AI at OpenAI, called it "superhuman pen-test at the scale of automated continuous scanning." Red Team also helps security teams validate vulnerabilities reported by code scanners, bug bounty programs and disclosure reports, and then test the patches for them.

Daybreak Defense Factory automates what OpenAI calls the "defensive loop": finding, validating and fixing vulnerabilities at scale. Its agents are built on OpenAI's latest cyber model, currently GPT-6 Cyber. They scan a codebase, hunt for vulnerabilities and develop patches. Engineers review and approve the proposed fixes before they go into production. "This way engineers get a merge-ready pull request with the patch and a test that shows that it works," Wang said.

## The pitch and the pushback

The Register framed the launch critically, noting that the company selling the defense also builds the kind of models that make attacks easier. The capabilities are OpenAI's own description of its tools. No independent evaluation was presented, and Red Team is not generally available.

On the same day, a coalition of four nonprofits, among them Public Citizen, filed a lawsuit in San Francisco Superior Court. They ask a judge to stop OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Meta and SpaceX's AI businesses from developing or deploying systems more capable than their current most advanced models, and cite AI-driven cyberattacks among their reasons.

The human step stays in place. Defense Factory proposes, engineers decide. A test bundled with a patch shows the fix works for the case it covers, not that the whole change is safe.

## What security teams can check now

Red Team is aimed first at teams that already run code scanners or a bug bounty program, since it is designed to validate the reports those sources produce and to test the fixes. Access runs through early access, so it is worth checking whether the program covers your web apps before planning around it.

For Defense Factory, review is the deciding point. The pull requests arrive merge-ready, but approval stays with engineers. Reading the patch and checking that the test would fail without it is the same work a reviewer does for any change. Brockman's own caveat applies here as well: fundamentals such as access control and code review do not disappear because an agent writes the fix.

## OpenAI startet zwei Daybreak-Sicherheitsprodukte

OpenAI hat zwei neue Sicherheitsprodukte vorgestellt, eines für Penetrationstests und eines für die Abwehr. Beide gehören zur Sicherheitsplattform Daybreak und wurden am 12. November 2026 auf einer Keynote präsentiert, wie The Register noch am selben Abend berichtete.

OpenAI-Präsident Greg Brockman nutzte den Auftritt für eine steile These: Unternehmen seien inzwischen nur noch so sicher wie das Frontier-Modell, mit dem sie sich verteidigen, und wie gut sie es einsetzen. Die Grundlagen der Sicherheit seien zwar wichtig und nicht zu unterschätzen. Firmen müssten ihre Sicherheitsarbeit aber grundlegend daran ausrichten, was diese Modelle können.

## Red Team greift an, Defense Factory repariert

Daybreak Red Team ist im Early Access verfügbar. Das Produkt testet die Web-Anwendungen eines Unternehmens mit OpenAI-Modellen auf Schwachstellen: Eine Flotte von Agents wertet Quellcode und App-Kontext aus und probiert mögliche Angriffswege durch. Nancy Wang, bei OpenAI für angewandte KI in der Cybersicherheit zuständig, sprach von einem „übermenschlichen Pen-Test im Maßstab automatisierter Dauer-Scans“. Außerdem hilft Red Team Sicherheitsteams, gemeldete Lücken aus Code-Scannern, Bug-Bounty-Programmen und Disclosure-Meldungen zu bestätigen und die zugehörigen Patches zu testen.

Daybreak Defense Factory automatisiert, was OpenAI den „defensiven Kreislauf“ nennt: Schwachstellen in großem Maßstab finden, bestätigen und beheben. Die Agents laufen auf OpenAIs jüngstem Cyber-Modell, derzeit GPT-6 Cyber. Sie durchsuchen Codebasen nach Lücken und entwickeln Patches. Bevor ein Fix in die Produktion geht, prüfen und genehmigen ihn Entwickler. „So bekommen Engineers einen Merge-fertigen Pull Request mit dem Patch und einem Test, der zeigt, dass er funktioniert“, sagte Wang.

## Verkaufsargument und Gegenwind

The Register ordnete den Start kritisch ein und wies darauf hin, dass ausgerechnet der Anbieter der Abwehr jene Art von Modellen baut, die Angriffe erleichtern. Die Fähigkeiten der Produkte beschreibt OpenAI selbst. Eine unabhängige Prüfung wurde nicht vorgelegt, und Red Team ist nicht allgemein verfügbar.

Am selben Tag reichten vier gemeinnützige Organisationen, darunter Public Citizen, Klage beim San Francisco Superior Court ein. Sie wollen OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Meta und die KI-Sparte von SpaceX gerichtlich daran hindern lassen, Systeme zu entwickeln oder einzusetzen, die leistungsfähiger sind als ihre derzeit stärksten Modelle. Als einen Grund nennen sie KI-gestützte Cyberangriffe.

Der menschliche Schritt bleibt. Defense Factory schlägt vor, Entwickler entscheiden. Ein mitgelieferter Test belegt, dass der Fix für den getesteten Fall greift, nicht aber, dass die ganze Änderung unbedenklich ist.

## Was Sicherheitsteams jetzt prüfen können

Red Team richtet sich zuerst an Teams, die bereits Code-Scanner oder ein Bug-Bounty-Programm betreiben, denn es soll deren Meldungen bestätigen und die Fixes testen. Der Zugang läuft über Early Access. Ob das Programm die eigenen Web-Apps abdeckt, sollte man vor jeder Planung klären.

Bei Defense Factory entscheidet das Review. Die Pull Requests kommen Merge-fertig, die Freigabe bleibt aber bei den Entwicklern. Den Patch lesen und prüfen, ob der Test ohne den Fix fehlschlagen würde, ist dieselbe Arbeit wie bei jeder anderen Änderung. Brockmans eigener Einwand gilt auch hier: Grundlagen wie Zugriffsrechte und Code-Review fallen nicht weg, nur weil ein Agent den Fix schreibt.

## Google adds a fast Gemini 4 model

Google introduced Gemini 4 Hydrogen on 12 November 2026. In the announcement, Koray Kavukcuoglu, Google's chief AI architect, describes it as bringing "speed and efficiency for everyday coding and agentic workflows." The larger frontier models, Gemini 4 Carbon and Gemini 4 Argon, remain Google's choice for deep, long-horizon reasoning on the hardest problems.

Hydrogen is rolling out globally from today. It is available in Google AI Studio, the Gemini API, Gemini for business, the Gemini app and Google Search, and for paid Google AI Pro and Ultra subscribers in Google Antigravity, the company's coding environment. Gemini in Google Sheets gets it first on AI Pro, Ultra and eligible business plans. Free users of the Gemini app get Hydrogen only through automatic model selection, when Google judges it the right model for the prompt.

Pricing is flat across the full 1-million-token context window: $1.50 per million input tokens and $7.50 per million output tokens. The model can also write up to 1 million output tokens.

## Four thinking levels and a model switcher

Hydrogen offers four thinking levels: low, medium, high (the default) and a new xhigh. Google says they scale smoothly, so you only wait and pay for the reasoning depth a task needs. At high, Hydrogen scores 51 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, against 50 for Argon. At xhigh it reaches 54.

Against Gemini 3.8 Flash, the model it is meant to replace for many teams, Google reports tasks finishing 2.5 times faster, Terminal-Bench 4.1 rising from 18.2 to 57 percent, and fabricated claims falling by more than five times. The model also adapts when a tool call fails or a search comes back empty, according to the post.

Alongside the model, Google is launching Orchestrator in Antigravity. Instead of using one model from start to finish, it switches between Carbon and Hydrogen within the same session. On Terminal-Bench 4.0, Google says, it came close to Carbon's success rate while using 24 percent less quota and finishing 19 percent faster on average. For parallel work, Carbon can coordinate while Hydrogen runs the worker and verifier agents.

In the Gemini app, Hydrogen is meant to follow tone, format and rules more closely and to call the right tools more often, including with context from Gmail and Google Drive. In Search, Google is upgrading its query fan-out technique to surface a broader range of links.

## Every benchmark comes from Google

All the numbers in the announcement are Google's own, and the post cites no independent rerun. A one-point lead over Argon on a general index says little about any single task. The same goes for the safety section. Google reports up to 81 percent less overreach in agentic tasks, a twelvefold drop in misaligned actions and shortcuts on its tool-use and coding evaluations, and 2.3 times more resilience against indirect prompt injection on the Gray Swan IPI benchmark. Each comparison is against Gemini 3.8 Flash, with details in the model card.

Access is uneven, too. Search is upgraded for all users, but free accounts in the Gemini app cannot pick Hydrogen themselves, and Sheets and Antigravity start on paid plans. "Available to everyone today" means different things depending on the account and the product.

## Where Hydrogen runs today

Developers can call Hydrogen through the Gemini API and try it in AI Studio. Google aims its migration figures squarely at teams on Gemini 3.8 Flash, and rerunning an existing workload at the new flat price is the quickest way to check the speed and cost claims.

With AI Pro or Ultra, Hydrogen shows up in the Gemini app's model menu, in Sheets and in Antigravity, where Orchestrator can be tried on a real project. Everyone else meets the model in Google Search, which Google says now copes better with multi-part questions and typos and links out to a wider range of sites.

## Hydrogen is Gemini 4's execution model

Google's 12 November 2026 announcement splits the Gemini 4 line by role. Carbon and Argon are the frontier models that "excel at deep, long-horizon reasoning on your hardest problems." Hydrogen "is built for rapid execution across diverse agentic workflows": writing code, running tests, verifying changes. Google positions it both as a standalone model and as the high-efficiency execution engine next to Carbon and Argon.

Pricing is flat across the full 1-million-token context window at $1.50 per million input tokens and $7.50 per million output tokens, with up to 1 million output tokens. Hydrogen is available in the Gemini API through AI Studio and Android Studio, in Gemini for business, the Gemini app and Google Search, and for AI Pro and Ultra subscribers in Google Antigravity.

## Thinking levels, parallel tool calls, Orchestrator

Four thinking levels (low, medium, high as the default, and the new xhigh) trade quality against latency and cost. Google calls the progression smooth and predictable. On the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, Hydrogen scores 51 at high and 54 at xhigh. Argon scores 50.

For teams migrating from Gemini 3.8 Flash, Google reports 2.5x faster completion at high, Terminal-Bench 4.1 at 57 percent versus 18.2, more than 5x fewer fabricated claims, and clean recovery when a tool call fails or a search returns empty. On large repositories the model batches file reads and search calls in parallel. In early testing, partners saw 2x to 2.8x speedups and 12 to 23 percent fewer tokens than with 3.8 Flash on graph, SQL and data-heavy workloads. Further claims include fifth place on arena.ai's Agent Arena, 58.8 percent on HLE-Diamond and 53.4 percent on the new Multimodal Knowledge Agent benchmark.

Orchestrator in Antigravity switches models dynamically within a session instead of pinning one. On Terminal-Bench 4.0, Google says it reached near-Carbon task success while using 24 percent less quota and finishing 19 percent faster on average. For parallel agents, Carbon coordinates while Hydrogen powers worker and verifier agents in isolated workspaces.

The safety section follows the same pattern: up to 81 percent less overreach and up to 79 percent less under-service in agentic tasks, a 12x reduction in misaligned actions and task shortcutting across tool-use and coding evaluations, and 2.3x more resilience against indirect prompt injection on the Gray Swan IPI benchmark. "Up to" marks the best case. Google refers to the model card for detail.

Routing is uneven. Free Gemini app users get Hydrogen only through automatic model selection, and Sheets and Antigravity start on paid tiers. Seeing Hydrogen on one surface says nothing about which model answers on another.

## Benchmark it on your own workload

The direct test is the migration itself. Run an existing 3.8 Flash workload against Hydrogen at low and high, and compare latency, output tokens and cost at the flat rate. Include a deliberately failing tool call and an empty search result, since recovery from both is one of Google's specific claims. If you run multi-step coding agents, check whether parallel file reads actually cut tokens on your repository. On a Pro or Ultra plan, compare Orchestrator's quota use against a Carbon-only run of the same task.

deepDiveMarkdown:
## OpenAI adds a central stop

As its models get more powerful, OpenAI says it has become more critical to detect problems and "quickly stop models in their tracks." Its answer is Control Room, a central system that tracks model workloads across the company's research infrastructure and stops them when safety or security concerns arise. OpenAI described it in a blog post on 12 November 2026.

Control Room covers every research inference workload, from agentic sampling for training and evaluation to data processing. According to OpenAI, it halts model output within 35 seconds of a decision to stop or pause a job, and it is already deployed across research, "where the need is greatest." ChatGPT and the API are not part of it. OpenAI says that external serving stack is more centralized already and can be taken down quickly.

## Engines ask before they answer

Three parts work together: the job a research team runs, the inference engine that runs the model on GPUs, and the Control Room service. Every research workload that does agentic inference must be tied to an approved safety case.

When a job starts, its code requests a job_id from Control Room. Each time it needs tokens, it calls an engine directly and passes that id along. Before fulfilling the request, the engine asks Control Room whether the job is still authorized. Once a person or a monitoring system has stopped the job, the answer is no, and the engine returns a refusal instead of output. The job's process may keep running, and the engine keeps serving other jobs.

All of OpenAI's frontier reinforcement learning jobs run with a monitor. That is another model which inspects everything the model in training does and raises an alert when it sees a problem. Depending on severity, the monitor can send the job_id to Control Room itself. OpenAI says a monitor caught its recent DNS-related incident.

## Fail closed, with a cache lag

The 35 seconds are the maximum between Control Room receiving a stop and the job being unable to make further progress. The delay comes from a caching layer for authorization checks, needed to handle the volume of traffic. OpenAI says it is working to bring it down to zero.

The check sits in the inference layer on purpose. Workload code changes often and is "not an ideal place" for load-bearing safety protections, while only a very small number of inference code paths exist across OpenAI research. Sweeps look for rogue engines launched without Control Room. And the system fails closed: if the service errors, is disabled or is tampered with, all inference requests are denied until it recovers. That is live for frontier-model research workloads and is due to reach the rest over the next few days.

## What the design shows

The timings and the coverage are OpenAI's own account. The post does not mention an outside audit, and it does not cover agents that customers run. What carries over is the pattern: every run gets an identifier, the stop lives where output is produced, and an outage blocks output instead of waving it through. OpenAI calls Control Room one part of a wider safety approach and plans to expand it over the coming months, alongside its monitoring for misaligned behavior and security breaches.

de.deepDiveMarkdown:
## OpenAI baut einen zentralen Stopp

Je leistungsfähiger die Modelle werden, desto wichtiger sei es, Probleme zu erkennen und Modelle schnell zu stoppen, schreibt OpenAI. Dafür hat das Unternehmen Control Room gebaut: ein zentrales System, das Modell-Workloads in der gesamten Forschungsinfrastruktur erfasst und anhält, sobald Sicherheitsbedenken aufkommen. Vorgestellt hat OpenAI es am 12. November 2026 in einem Blogbeitrag.

Angebunden ist jeder Inference-Workload der Forschung, vom agentischen Sampling für Training und Evaluation bis zur Datenverarbeitung. Nach der Entscheidung, einen Job zu stoppen oder zu pausieren, endet die Modellausgabe laut OpenAI binnen 35 Sekunden. Im Einsatz ist das System bereits in der Forschung, wo der Bedarf am größten sei. Der Stack hinter ChatGPT und der API gehört nicht dazu. Er sei ohnehin zentraler aufgebaut und lasse sich schnell abschalten.

## Die Engine fragt vor jeder Antwort

Drei Teile greifen ineinander: der Job eines Forschungsteams, die Inference-Engine, die das Modell auf GPUs ausführt, und der Control-Room-Dienst. Jeder Forschungs-Workload mit agentischer Inference muss an einen genehmigten Safety Case gebunden sein.

Beim Start fordert der Job-Code eine job_id bei Control Room an. Braucht er Token, ruft er eine Engine direkt auf und übergibt die Kennung. Bevor die Engine liefert, fragt sie Control Room, ob der Job noch freigegeben ist. Hat ein Mensch oder ein Monitoring-System den Job gestoppt, lautet die Antwort nein, und die Engine schickt eine Ablehnung statt Ausgabe. Der Prozess selbst darf weiterlaufen, die Engine bedient andere Jobs weiter.

Alle Frontier-Jobs im Reinforcement Learning laufen bei OpenAI mit einem Monitor. Das ist ein weiteres Modell, das alles beobachtet, was das trainierte Modell tut, und bei Problemen Alarm schlägt. Je nach Schwere kann der Monitor die job_id selbst an Control Room schicken. Den jüngsten DNS-Vorfall habe ein solcher Monitor entdeckt.

## Ein Ausfall sperrt alles

Die 35 Sekunden sind die maximale Zeit zwischen dem Eingang eines Stoppbefehls bei Control Room und dem Moment, ab dem der Job nicht mehr weiterkommt. Die Verzögerung entsteht durch eine Cache-Schicht für die Freigabeprüfungen, die das hohe Anfragevolumen abfängt. OpenAI arbeitet nach eigenen Angaben daran, sie auf null zu senken.

Dass die Prüfung in der Inference-Schicht sitzt, ist Absicht. Der Code der Workloads ändert sich häufig und eignet sich laut OpenAI schlecht für tragende Schutzmechanismen. Inference-Codepfade gibt es dagegen nur sehr wenige. Zusätzlich suchen Sweeps nach Engines, die ohne Control Room gestartet wurden. Und das System ist „fail closed“: Hat der Dienst einen Fehler, wird er abgeschaltet oder manipuliert, lehnen die Engines jede Anfrage ab, bis er wieder läuft. Für Forschungs-Workloads mit Frontier-Modellen gilt das schon, der Rest soll in den nächsten Tagen folgen.

## Was der Ansatz zeigt

Zeiten und Reichweite beschreibt OpenAI selbst, eine externe Prüfung erwähnt der Beitrag nicht. Agents, die Kunden betreiben, deckt Control Room nicht ab. Übertragbar ist das Muster: Jeder Lauf bekommt eine Kennung, der Stopp sitzt dort, wo die Ausgabe entsteht, und ein Ausfall blockiert, statt durchzulassen. OpenAI nennt Control Room einen Baustein seines Sicherheitsansatzes und will das System in den kommenden Monaten ausbauen, parallel zur Überwachung auf Misalignment und Sicherheitslücken.

## Revocation for research inference

OpenAI's Control Room, described on 12 November 2026, is a central authorization service for model workloads across the company's research infrastructure. It covers every research inference workload, including agentic sampling for training and evaluation, high-volume sampling and data processing. OpenAI says it halts model output within 35 seconds of a decision to stop or pause a job, keeps working when other systems fail, and stops output if Control Room itself goes down.

The scope is research, "where the need is greatest." OpenAI's external serving stack for ChatGPT and the API is out of scope. The company describes it as already centralized, with a well-developed ability to take deployments down quickly.

## A job_id check per request

The system has three parts: the workload, the inference engine and the Control Room service. Every research workload doing agentic inference must be associated with an approved safety case. At startup, workload code requests a job_id. Sampling calls go straight to an engine with that id and never pass through Control Room. The engine forwards the id, asks for permission and only then fulfills the request.

A stop from a person or a monitor marks the id as terminated. The workload process can stay alive, because OpenAI does not rely on it to check its own status. The next request is denied and the engine returns a refusal instead of tokens, while it keeps serving other authorized jobs. A workload may use several engines and an engine may serve several workloads, so the id is what gets revoked. Every frontier reinforcement learning job runs with a monitor model that can, depending on severity, send the stop itself.

## Cache lag and fail-closed

The 35 seconds are the maximum between Control Room receiving a stop and the point where further progress is impossible. The lag comes from a caching layer for inference authorization, sized for traffic volume, and OpenAI says it is working to drive it to zero.

The reasoning for the placement is operational. Workload code is varied, decentralized and changes often, so OpenAI considers it a poor home for load-bearing safety controls. Only a very small number of inference code paths exist in research, deployed centrally and uniformly, which makes the inference layer a bottleneck where every request can be checked. Continual agentic and programmatic sweeps look for engines launched with Control Room unimplemented or disabled. If the service errors, is disabled or is tampered with, engines deny all inference until it recovers. Fail-closed is rolled out for frontier-model research workloads and is due across the remaining ones over the next few days.

## Limits of the claim

Bounds, coverage and rollout status are OpenAI's own statements, and no external audit is cited. Customer-run agents are not covered. Fail-closed also means an outage halts authorized jobs, a trade-off the post accepts without quantifying it. For teams running agent infrastructure, the transferable parts are a per-run identity, revocation checked on the serving path, a known bound on cached allows, and denial when the authorization service is unreachable. OpenAI says it will expand Control Room over the coming months alongside its monitoring for misalignment and security breaches.

Widerrufen wird deshalb die Kennung. Jeder Frontier-Job im Reinforcement Learning läuft mit einem Monitor-Modell, das je nach Schwere den Stopp selbst auslösen kann.

Die 35 Sekunden sind die maximale Zeit zwischen dem Eingang eines Stopps bei Control Room und dem Punkt, ab dem kein Fortschritt mehr möglich ist. Sie stammen aus einer Cache-Schicht für die Inference-Freigabe, ausgelegt auf das Anfragevolumen. OpenAI will die Verzögerung auf null drücken.

## United shuts out personal AI agents

United Airlines is restricting access for unauthorized third-party AI agents. The airline announced the step on 11 November 2026. It applies directly on united.com and in the United app, and indirectly through travel agencies and aggregators. United is updating its booking, ticketing and distribution policies to match.

The airline gives three reasons. Sharing account credentials with a personal AI assistant can expose sensitive information. Actions the tools take can lead to unintended purchases, account changes or the use of MileagePlus miles. And automated actions could violate FAA and DOT regulations: check-in, United notes, requires a human to acknowledge that bags contain no banned substances such as explosives.

## What counts as unauthorized

United's Digital Trust Center spells out the test. If an AI agent, bot, browser extension or browser feature searches, books, buys, manages or collects information on united.com or in the app without United's permission, it is unauthorized. Giving the tool access yourself does not change that. "Just because you've given access to AI assistants doesn't mean United will permit an AI assistant to transact with United," the FAQ says.

Research is still fine. AI can help plan a trip as long as it does not access United's site or app, and according to The Wall Street Journal, agents can still show United flights and fares. Assistive technology for customers with disabilities is not affected. Travel agencies may use their own AI tools only with United's permission. United says it does not work with any third-party agents yet.

## The contract of carriage backs it up

The revised contract of carriage defines an AI agent broadly: any software that takes autonomous or semi-autonomous action to search, book, ticket or manage a trip, whether or not a passenger supervises or approves it. Reservations made, modified or serviced by AI agents are now on the list of bookings United may cancel without notice. Existing trips get more leeway. United is seeing little booking activity from agents so far, and its systems can tell whether a reservation came from a traveler, a travel agency or an automated assistant, the Journal reports. Chief executive Scott Kirby was blunter at an event in Chicago: "To be honest, I don't want to create another middleman." The Verge notes that eBay and several major banks have also restricted agents.

If an assistant holds your MileagePlus login, change the password. Don't hand a third-party agent confirmation numbers or MileagePlus details. Review any trip an agent booked for you. From here on, the split at United is simple: the AI may research, but the booking happens on united.com or in the app, by you.

## Eine Vertriebsregel, keine Designfrage

United hat am 11. November 2026 angekündigt, nicht autorisierte KI-Agents von Drittanbietern direkt auf den eigenen digitalen Plattformen und indirekt über Reisebüros und Buchungsportale einzuschränken. Umgesetzt wird das über die Regeln für Buchung, Ticketing und Vertrieb. Die Pressemitteilung nennt als Risiken offengelegte Zugangsdaten, ungewollte Käufe, Kontoänderungen und eingelöste MileagePlus-Meilen. Dazu kommt ein regulatorisches: Beim Check-in muss ein Mensch bestätigen, dass im Gepäck keine verbotenen Stoffe sind, und automatisierte Aktionen könnten laut United gegen Vorschriften von FAA und DOT verstoßen.

## Die Beförderungsbedingungen definieren den Agent

Die überarbeiteten Beförderungsbedingungen definieren einen KI-Agent als jede Software oder jeden Dienst, der autonom oder teilautonom Produkte findet, sucht, bucht, kauft, ausstellt, betreut oder verwaltet, unabhängig davon, ob der Passagier dabei zusieht oder zustimmt. Ausdrücklich erfasst sind Assistenten in Social-Media-, Messaging- und Suchplattformen, KI-Browser, eigenständige Agents und Assistenten, die über Tools oder Anbindungen eines Reisebüros auf United zugreifen. Reservierungen, die ein KI-Agent anlegt, ändert oder betreut, stehen nun auf der Liste der Buchungen, die United ohne Vorwarnung stornieren darf.

Das Digital Trust Center übersetzt die Regel in die Praxis. Jeder Agent, Bot, jede Browser-Erweiterung oder Browser-Funktion, die ohne Erlaubnis von United auf united.com oder in der App handelt, gilt als unerlaubt. Die Zustimmung der Nutzer ersetzt diese Erlaubnis nicht. Recherche, die United-Seiten nicht berührt, bleibt erlaubt, Hilfstechnik für Menschen mit Behinderung ist ausgenommen, und Reisebüros dürfen eigene KI-Tools nur mit Zustimmung von United einsetzen. Integrationen mit Agents von Drittanbietern gibt es laut United noch nicht. Zuerst will die Airline standardisierte, sichere Anbindungen mit Schutz für Privatsphäre, Sicherheit, Berechtigungen und Verantwortlichkeit.

## Erkennung und Motiv

Nach Angaben des Wall Street Journal kann United in seinen Systemen unterscheiden, ob eine Reservierung von Reisenden, klassischen Reisebüros oder automatisierten Assistenten stammt, und sieht bislang wenig Buchungen durch Agents. Wie diese Zuordnung funktioniert, erklären weder Pressemitteilung noch Trust Center. View from the Wing weist darauf hin, dass ein Agent, der über ein Online-Reisebüro kauft, bei United womöglich nur als Buchung dieses Reisebüros ankommt. Ein vertragliches Verbot ist noch keine technische Sperre.

Kirbys Bemerkung in Chicago, er wolle ehrlich gesagt keinen weiteren Zwischenhändler schaffen, ergänzt die Sicherheitsbegründung um ein kommerzielles Motiv. Laut Journal streiten Airlines seit Jahren mit Online-Reisebüros darüber, wie ihre Tarife angezeigt und verkauft werden. The Verge verweist auf ähnliche Beschränkungen bei eBay und mehreren großen Banken.

## Suche ja, Abschluss beim Nutzer

Für Teams, die Reise-Agents bauen, ist die Linie klar. Suche und Preisanzeige werden geduldet, die Ausführung nicht. Kauf, Check-in und Umbuchung sollten an united.com oder die App übergeben werden, MileagePlus-Zugangsdaten und Buchungsnummern gehören nicht in den Agent. Reisebüros brauchen die Erlaubnis von United, bevor ein KI-Tool auf direkten oder indirekten Wegen bucht. Agent-Buchungen von vor dem 11. November 2026 bleiben bestehen, United empfiehlt aber zu prüfen, ob sie korrekt gebucht und ausgestellt wurden.

## Gemini Live moves to the car display

Google is bringing the Gemini app to Apple CarPlay. Announced on 11 November 2026, the feature lets iOS users have "natural, free-flowing conversations" with Gemini Live right from their car's display, hands-free. It follows Google's rollout on Android Auto and in cars with Google built-in.

Google pitches it as a use for commute time. Voice assistants have long handled quick tasks like playing a playlist or getting directions home, the company writes; the quiet time on the road is also a chance to catch up, prepare for what's ahead or simply think out loud.

## How it works

Tapping the Gemini icon on the CarPlay screen or side rail opens a recent chat or starts a new one. The conversation runs at your own pace: you can interrupt to add a detail, change the subject, or pause when you need to focus on an exit. Google says it designed the app as "a conversational driving companion that minimizes distraction."

Because Gemini connects to Google Workspace apps such as Gmail and Google Calendar, it can tell you what's on your calendar and when to leave for your next appointment, catch you up on unread email, summarize long threads and help you talk through a quick reply. Google also suggests asking for lunch spots or the backstory of a local landmark, and using the car as a place to rehearse: one sample prompt asks Gemini to roleplay a skeptical VP and challenge a Q4 pitch.

Conversations sync automatically with the Gemini app on the iPhone, so summaries and notes are in the chat history once you park.

## Rollout and limits

Gemini on CarPlay is rolling out globally starting 11 November to all Gemini users on iOS, in every language Gemini Live supports. A global rollout means it may take some time before the icon shows up on every phone. Google lists three requirements: the latest version of the Gemini app, microphone permissions, and at least one use of Gemini Live on the phone.

## Daily Brief is off in the EEA

One feature is restricted. According to Google's footnote, Daily Brief has to be enabled first, and certain personalization features, including Daily Brief, are not available to users under 18 or in the European Economic Area and Nigeria. That includes Germany. The conversation itself is not affected by that restriction.

Google's claim that the app minimizes distraction describes its design goal. The announcement does not include data on driver attention.

deepDiveMarkdown:
## Decisions instead of answers

Google introduced the Gemini Decisions API on 11 November 2026, a new endpoint for "fast, closed-set decisions" in the Gemini API and Google AI Studio. It runs on a new model, Gemini Decision 1 (gemini-decision-1). Google pitches it for bounded choices: tool selection, policy checks, model routing and grading context.

A request takes one multimodal input of up to 256K tokens, mixing text, images, audio, video and PDFs, along with up to 1,000 independent questions. Google's examples include a call recording paired with account metadata, or a scanned PDF claim with damage photos.

## Scored in a single pass

Rather than generating answer text token by token, Gemini Decision 1 scores the candidate options in a single forward pass. Three question types can be mixed in one request: yes/no checks, multiple choice with 2 to 255 options, and scores on an ordered rubric that starts at 0. Each answer comes with a confidence score between 0 and 1, so code can route ambiguous cases to a fallback or a human reviewer.

Google's sample checks a photo of a breakroom counter, together with a note about a 9 a.m. client meeting. One request asks whether there is an uncleaned spill, which cleanup action fits, and how severe the mess is.

According to Google, end-to-end latency is 150 to 250 ms. Median model compute is 50 to 100 ms and stays nearly flat from 1 to 100 questions, measured on inputs up to 16K tokens. The shared input is billed once per request, and each extra question adds only its own instruction and criteria tokens.

## Google's numbers, Google's tests

Google says Gemini Decision 1 leads its benchmark suite across agent routing, reasoning, ranking and multimodal understanding, with the lowest calibration error. On that suite it is described as nearly five times cheaper than Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite through the Interactions API. These are vendor results, and the post cites no independent evaluation. The flat-latency figure also covers a narrower range than the maximum of 1,000 questions and 256K tokens.

The trade-off is built in. The model does not explain its choice, and it can only pick among options that were defined in advance.

## Already in Google products

Google says teams inside the company already use the API. Gemini Notebook routes queries to the right model tier with up to 40 percent lower latency on everyday requests, CC from Google Labs picks emoji reactions from more than 200 options, and Google Search uses it as a safety layer for MCP tools.

Pricing is $0.10 per million input tokens and nothing for output, with a no-cost tier in AI Studio for prototyping. Integrations with common developer frameworks are rolling out, and support in Gemini in Google Cloud is coming soon.

## A closed-set decision endpoint

Google released the Gemini Decisions API on 11 November 2026, a new endpoint in the Gemini API built on Gemini Decision 1 (gemini-decision-1). It offers "purpose-built primitives for bounded choices": tool selection, policy checks, model routing and context grading. One request carries a single multimodal input of up to 256K tokens across text, images, audio, video and PDFs, plus up to 1,000 independent questions.

The input field uses the same Content block format as the Interactions API. Resolution on image and video inputs is tunable, trading visual detail against token cost.

## One forward pass, no decode

Gemini Decision 1 scores candidate options in a single forward pass instead of decoding text. The yes/no type estimates the probability that a condition holds, with optional true and false criteria. Choice selects from 2 to 255 options and returns the winner with normalized probabilities for every candidate. Score grades against an ordered rubric starting at 0 and returns a continuous weighted score plus per-level probabilities. Every answer carries a confidence from 0 to 1 for routing ambiguous cases to a fallback or human review.

Google reports median model compute of 50 to 100 ms, nearly flat from 1 to 100 questions, on contexts up to 16K tokens, and 150 to 250 ms end to end. Billing follows the architecture: the shared input is charged once per request, each question adds only its instruction and criteria tokens, and there are no output, thinking, transcription or OCR charges.

## Vendor benchmarks, narrow ranges

Google says Gemini Decision 1 leads a suite spanning agent routing, reasoning, ranking and multimodal understanding, with the lowest calibration error, and is nearly 5x cheaper on that suite than Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite via the Interactions API. No independent evaluation is cited. The latency figures cover 16K-token contexts and up to 100 questions, well below the 256K-token, 1,000-question ceiling, and Google gives no numbers for the upper end.

The output is a distribution, not a rationale. Because choice probabilities are normalized across the options provided, scope checks and thresholds belong in calling code.

## Google runs it as a control plane

Internally, Google describes the API as a low-latency control plane. Gemini Notebook routes queries to a model tier and thinking level, with up to 40 percent lower latency on everyday queries. Stitch uses it for a rapid canvas experiment, CC from Google Labs picks reactions from more than 200 emoji, and Google Search uses it to detect adversarial behavior around MCP tools.

Pricing is $0.10 per million input tokens and $0 for output, with a no-cost tier in AI Studio. Python, JavaScript and REST guides are available, framework integrations are rolling out, and support in Gemini in Google Cloud is coming soon.

deepDiveMarkdown:
## From tissues to single cells

Every cell in the body carries the same DNA, yet a heart muscle cell and an immune cell switch different genes on and off. Predicting how subtle DNA variations change that activity in specific cells is still an unsolved problem. On 11 November 2026 Google DeepMind announced AlphaGenome 2, a model built for exactly that.

The first AlphaGenome, launched last year, predicted variant effects across broad tissues. AlphaGenome 2 zooms in to individual cell types and states. DeepMind says it identifies nearly twice as many variants that change gene expression in cells as its previous state-of-the-art model.

## One condition at a time

The original model took a million-letter DNA sequence and predicted thousands of experiments across many tissues in parallel. DeepMind says that spread its capacity thin. AlphaGenome 2 is a conditional model: alongside the DNA sequence, it takes one target condition as input at every stage, whether a tissue, a cell type or a state. That lets it learn how the same stretch of DNA is read differently in different cells.

It was trained on bulk and single-cell data from human and mouse samples, including over 107 million individual cell profiles. Besides gene expression, histone modifications and chromatin accessibility, it now also predicts DNA methylation. Because it separates a cell's state from its outputs, it can fill in missing measurements, for example predicting chromatin accessibility from single-cell gene activity.

Scientists can upload a single-cell RNA-seq snapshot from a few dozen cells, and the model adapts to that new state without retraining. On data from a COVID-19 mRNA vaccine study it had not seen, it told vaccine-activated T cells from resting ones and found that a variant linked to severe COVID-19 disrupts gene activity more strongly in the activated state.

## Strong results, research use only

On TenK10K, a single-cell map of 28 immune cell types, AlphaGenome 2 identified 30 percent of causal variants against 16 percent for the original model fine-tuned on single-cell data, and 43 against 23 percent of directional gene effects. It also reproduced a known finding: a distant regulatory variant drives inflammatory bowel disease by overactivating the ETS2 gene in gut macrophages.

These results come from DeepMind's own evaluation. DeepMind stresses that AlphaGenome and AlphaGenome 2 are for research only and have not been validated or approved for clinical or diagnostic purposes.

## How researchers get access

AlphaGenome 2 is available now for non-commercial research through the AlphaGenome API, with Colab tutorials, and in private preview for commercial research. DeepMind has precomputed predictions for trait-associated variants across hundreds of human cell and tissue conditions, so researchers can link GWAS findings to cell types without running the computation themselves. AlphaGenome 2 Skills for Antigravity, Google's agentic development platform, are due soon.

## Vom Gewebe zur einzelnen Zelle

Jede Zelle im Körper trägt dieselbe DNA, und doch schalten eine Herzmuskelzelle und eine Immunzelle unterschiedliche Gene an und aus. Vorherzusagen, wie kleine Abweichungen in der DNA diese Aktivität in bestimmten Zellen verändern, ist bislang ungelöst. Google DeepMind hat am 11. November 2026 AlphaGenome 2 vorgestellt, ein Modell genau für diese Aufgabe.

Das erste AlphaGenome kam im vergangenen Jahr und sagte Varianteneffekte für ganze Gewebe vorher. AlphaGenome 2 geht bis auf einzelne Zelltypen und Zellzustände hinunter. Nach Angaben von DeepMind erkennt es fast doppelt so viele Varianten, die die Genexpression in Zellen verändern, wie das bisherige Spitzenmodell.

## Ein Zustand nach dem anderen

Das ursprüngliche Modell nahm eine DNA-Sequenz von einer Million Buchstaben und sagte Tausende Experimente aus vielen Geweben gleichzeitig vorher. Das habe seine Kapazität zu dünn verteilt, schreibt DeepMind. AlphaGenome 2 ist ein konditionales Modell: Neben der DNA-Sequenz bekommt es in jeder Stufe seiner Architektur eine Zielbedingung, etwa ein Gewebe, einen Zelltyp oder einen Zustand. So lernt es, wie derselbe DNA-Abschnitt in verschiedenen Zellen unterschiedlich gelesen wird.

Trainiert wurde es auf Bulk- und Einzelzelldaten von Mensch und Maus, darunter mehr als 107 Millionen einzelne Zellprofile. Neben Genexpression, Histon-Modifikationen und Chromatin-Zugänglichkeit sagt es nun auch DNA-Methylierung vorher. Weil es den Zustand einer Zelle von den Messwerten trennt, kann es fehlende Messungen ergänzen und etwa aus der Genaktivität einzelner Zellen die Chromatin-Zugänglichkeit ableiten.

Forschende können einen Einzelzell-RNA-seq-Schnappschuss aus wenigen Dutzend Zellen hochladen, und das Modell stellt sich ohne neues Training auf diesen Zustand ein. Auf Daten einer Studie zum mRNA-Impfstoff gegen COVID-19, die es nicht kannte, unterschied es impfaktivierte T-Zellen von ruhenden. Zudem zeigte es, dass eine mit schweren COVID-19-Verläufen verknüpfte Variante die Genaktivität im aktivierten Zustand stärker stört.

## Starke Werte, nur für die Forschung

Auf TenK10K, einer Einzelzellkarte von 28 Immunzelltypen, fand AlphaGenome 2 30 Prozent der ursächlichen Varianten, das auf Einzelzelldaten feinjustierte Vorgängermodell 16 Prozent. Bei der Richtung der Geneffekte lag es bei 43 gegenüber 23 Prozent. Außerdem reproduzierte es einen bekannten Befund: Eine weit entfernte regulatorische Variante treibt chronisch-entzündliche Darmerkrankungen an, indem sie das Gen ETS2 in Makrophagen des Darms überaktiviert.

Die Ergebnisse stammen aus DeepMinds eigener Auswertung. DeepMind betont, dass AlphaGenome und AlphaGenome 2 nur für die Forschung gedacht und weder für klinische noch für diagnostische Zwecke validiert oder zugelassen sind.

## So kommen Forschende heran

AlphaGenome 2 steht ab sofort für nicht-kommerzielle Forschung über die AlphaGenome API bereit, samt Colab-Tutorials, für kommerzielle Forschung in einer privaten Vorschau. DeepMind hat Vorhersagen für merkmalsassoziierte Varianten in Hunderten menschlicher Zell- und Gewebezustände vorberechnet. So lassen sich GWAS-Treffer mit Zelltypen verknüpfen, ohne die Rechnung selbst aufzusetzen. AlphaGenome 2 Skills für Antigravity, Googles agentische Entwicklungsplattform, sollen bald folgen.

## From parallel tracks to conditioning

Google DeepMind announced AlphaGenome 2 on 11 November 2026 as a model that bridges single-cell biology and human genetics, predicting how variants affect hundreds of human cell types. The first AlphaGenome took a 1-million-letter DNA sequence and produced fixed parallel outputs for thousands of bulk-tissue and cell-line experiments at once. DeepMind says that design spread model capacity thin and made it hard to separate closely related cell types.

AlphaGenome 2 is conditional. It predicts for one condition at a time, whether a tissue, a cell type or a state, and feeds that condition into every stage of the architecture alongside the sequence. The condition comes either from a reference catalog or from a scientist's own single-cell experiment via a cell encoder.

## Training data and new readouts

The model was trained on bulk and single-cell human and mouse data, including over 107 million individual cell profiles. It keeps AlphaGenome's core readouts of gene expression, histone modifications and chromatin accessibility, and adds DNA methylation. Separating cell state from outputs enables cross-modality imputation: given only single-cell gene activity, it can predict unmeasured properties such as chromatin accessibility.

For unseen states, a single-cell RNA-seq snapshot of a few dozen cells is compressed into a cell-state representation that conditions the model. DeepMind says this matches or beats models trained or fine-tuned directly on those datasets. On unseen data from a COVID-19 mRNA vaccine study, it separated vaccine-activated T cells from resting ones and showed a severe-COVID variant disrupting gene activity more strongly in the activated state.

## Benchmarks and caveats

On genome regions outside its training data, AlphaGenome 2 explains significantly more of how expression differs across cell types within a tissue, including continuous trajectories in hematopoiesis. On TenK10K, 28 primary immune cell types, it recovers 30% of causal variants against 16% and 43% of directional gene effects against 23%, compared with AlphaGenome fine-tuned on single-cell data and other specialized tools. It also reproduced the ETS2 finding in IBD, singling out the causal distal variant and its macrophage-specific effect.

These evaluations are DeepMind's own. The company states that AlphaGenome and AlphaGenome 2 are for research use only and have not been validated or approved for clinical or diagnostic purposes.

## Access and precomputed scores

AlphaGenome 2 is available for non-commercial research via the AlphaGenome API, with Colab tutorials for expression conditioning, and in private preview for commercial research. DeepMind precomputed scores for trait-associated GWAS variants across hundreds of cell and tissue conditions, covering enhancer-gene links in primary cell types such as astrocytes and fine-mapping for traits from height to type 2 diabetes. ## Zugang und vorberechnete Scores

Sie decken Enhancer-Gen-Verknüpfungen in primären Zelltypen wie Astrozyten ab und helfen bei der Feinkartierung von Merkmalen von der Körpergröße bis zu Typ-2-Diabetes. AlphaGenome 2 Skills für Google Antigravity sind angekündigt.

## Adobe turns its apps into agentic workflows

Adobe announced a broad set of updates at its MAX conference in Miami Beach on 10 November 2026. The headline: the Adobe Creative Agent is expanding across Creative Cloud and now orchestrates multi-step workflows, so professionals can "delegate and direct work," as Adobe puts it. The company also previewed local MCP integrations that will let people use Creative Cloud tools from their preferred third-party agents.

"Our latest Creative Cloud innovations transform our trusted creative tools into agentic, intelligent workflows," said Deepa Subramaniam, vice president of product marketing for Creative Cloud.

## The agent inside the apps, and agents from outside

The Creative Agent is now available in Premiere, Illustrator, InDesign, After Effects and Frame.io. In Premiere, it can apply effects across every clip in a sequence, track masked subjects through a frame and adjust color and exposure across an entire sequence at once.

The MCP integrations go a step further. Third-party agents will be able to work locally in Photoshop, Illustrator, Premiere and After Effects and make changes directly in native project files on the user's computer. Adobe says layers, vectors, bins and sequences remain editable, and users can step in at any moment. An agent connected to other MCP-capable tools could, for example, pull a brief from Google Docs, work on the project in Adobe's apps and share the result in Slack.

In Firefly, Adobe introduced Firefly Design (beta), which brings illustration, image editing, animation, 3D and print onto one canvas; Firefly Graph (beta) for repeatable workflows that combine AI models with Adobe's production tools; and Firefly Builder (private beta) for turning ideas into interactive prototypes using natural language.

The AI Assistants powered by the Creative Agent are in beta in Adobe's flagship desktop apps; in Photoshop, the assistant is only available in the Photoshop beta app. Firefly Design and Firefly Graph are in beta, and Firefly Builder is in private beta. The local MCP integrations are a preview and will be available in private beta in early 2027.

Adobe stresses that professionals stay in control and decide when to hand tasks to AI and when to work by hand.

Alongside the agent features, Adobe added tools to its flagship apps. Photoshop gets Relight for adding and adjusting light and Generative Restyle, which turns prompt-based edits into adjustable sliders. Premiere gets Color Mode, a new color grading system, a Generative Media Tool for video, sound effects and music in the timeline, and Generative Remove in beta. Lightroom adds Glow, Blemish Removal and Open Eyes (beta), and InDesign gets real-time Co-editing in beta.

## Anthropic keeps the work inside Claude

Anthropic has introduced Claude Whiteboards and Claude Sheets in beta, and Claude Dashboards becomes generally available under a new name, Claude Data. All three are available on every paid plan.

The pitch is simple. Working on a project with Claude often meant moving the output into another tool, where Claude no longer had live access to follow changes. Now documents, boards, sheets and dashboards can stay in Claude, and the team can keep editing them together. When the work is ready, it can move on to partner tools.

## Boards, sheets and certified numbers

Whiteboards is a shared board where a team brainstorms with Claude. You can talk through a messy plan, and Claude turns it into a board with a timeline, owners and dates. In a retro, everyone adds notes, and Claude groups them by theme and drafts action items for each person. Dragging a box around part of the board focuses Claude's answers on that area. Afterwards, Claude can turn the board into a doc or deck, or hand it to Lucid, Miro or Vani by Zoho.

Sheets lets Claude generate spreadsheets with tabs, formulas, formatting and drop-downs, often from a single prompt such as a campaign tracker or a hiring budget. Claude edits cells directly and outlines each edit so changes stay traceable. Sheets can be shared, and teams can export to .xlsx or CSV or continue in Airtable, Asana, monday.com or Smartsheet.

Claude Data grew out of Claude Dashboards, which launched in beta in October for questions about company data in warehouses such as Amazon Redshift, BigQuery and ClickHouse. Anthropic renamed it because companies use data more broadly than dashboards. Data teams can now certify the queries everyone should use, and charts built on them carry a "certified" badge. Live sharing shows colleagues current numbers even if they lack access to the underlying connectors; viewers only see the results of approved queries. Claude can also draft data stories and narrated videos for review, and dashboards gain caching, design systems and tracked changes with rollback.

## Simple for now

Anthropic is open about the limits. Sheets offers "simple spreadsheet functionality" for now, with more to come. For the full feature set, it points to exporting to Excel or to Claude for Excel. Certified queries and live sharing are still in beta, and Claude Data only works with a data connector such as a warehouse or CRM.

## Who gets it and when

Whiteboards, Sheets and Data run on web, desktop and mobile. On Team plans, all three are on by default. On Enterprise plans, Whiteboards and Sheets start switched off, and Claude Data turns on by default on 19 November 2026. Admins can change this at any time under Organization settings > Artifacts.

Separately, interactive connectors can now open as full apps beside the conversation or in full screen, so tools like Adobe, Atlassian, Box and Notion can be used directly inside Claude.

deepDiveMarkdown:
## A voice that follows the speaker

DeepL has unveiled Aure, which the Cologne company calls its most dynamic and lifelike voice AI model yet. Announced on 11 November 2026, Aure powers DeepL Voice, DeepL's product for translating speech in real time. The model continuously adapts the translated speech to how someone is speaking, from shifts in tone and emotion to changes in emphasis and pace.

"Our voice is fundamental to who we are," said DeepL CEO and founder Jarek Kutylowski. With Aure, he said, the company can capture "even the subtlest shifts in expression as they happen" and carry them into another language, in the speaker's own voice.

Aure builds on DeepL's recent voice preservation feature, which lets people be heard in their own recognizable voice rather than a generic synthetic one. That preserved the identity of a voice. Aure is meant to capture how the voice changes over a conversation.

## From a snapshot to continuous analysis

Previously, DeepL Voice relied on the opening moments of a conversation to decide how a person's translated voice should sound. According to DeepL, that captured who was speaking, but not how. A fixed snapshot can't follow a change in emotion, emphasis or pace, or convey delivery that contradicts the words, such as sarcasm.

Aure analyzes incoming speech continuously and uses both the translated words and the source audio to shape how a sentence is delivered. DeepL names three problems it had to solve together. Real conversations are noisy, so the model has to isolate the speaker's voice and prosody from background noise, echo and distortion. Carrying a voice across languages without exaggerating accents is harder than within one language. And there is little real-world data of the same speaker in several languages, partly because DeepL Voice does not permanently store meeting transcripts or translations and deletes them from memory when a session ends. Aure therefore has to adapt to each speaker in real time, before a sentence is finished.

To get there, DeepL combined training techniques that separate voice identity, prosody and spoken content, so each can be carried into a new language independently. Reinforcement learning refines the output for translation accuracy and natural-sounding speech.

## Where it runs

Aure is applied automatically, with no configuration, in DeepL Voice for Online Meetings, DeepL Voice for In-Person Conversations and the DeepL API for Voice. It initially supports English, German, Spanish, French, Italian, Japanese, Portuguese and Korean, with more languages to follow; other languages keep using DeepL's existing voice models.

## What is still open

DeepL's examples come from work: a pause before an important announcement, urgency in a negotiation, a shift from serious to enthusiastic when good news reaches a global team. How reliably Aure carries those moments has not been tested independently. So far, the claims are DeepL's own.

## Eine Stimme, die dem Sprecher folgt

DeepL hat Aure vorgestellt, nach Angaben des Kölner Unternehmens sein bislang dynamischstes und lebensechtestes Voice-AI-Modell. Aure wurde am 11. November 2026 angekündigt und steckt in DeepL Voice, dem Produkt für Sprachübersetzung in Echtzeit. Das Modell passt die übersetzte Sprache laufend daran an, wie jemand spricht: an Wechsel in Tonfall und Emotion ebenso wie an Betonung und Tempo.

„Unsere Stimme ist grundlegend dafür, wer wir sind", sagt DeepL-Gründer und CEO Jarek Kutylowski. Mit Aure könne man selbst feinste Veränderungen im Ausdruck erfassen, während sie passieren, und in eine andere Sprache übertragen, in der eigenen Stimme des Sprechers.

Aure baut auf der Stimmerhaltung auf, die DeepL kürzlich eingeführt hat. Damit hört man Menschen in ihrer eigenen, wiedererkennbaren Stimme statt in einer generischen synthetischen. Das bewahrte die Identität einer Stimme. Aure soll nun erfassen, wie sie sich im Gespräch verändert.

## Von der Momentaufnahme zur laufenden Analyse

Bisher bestimmten die ersten Momente eines Gesprächs, wie die übersetzte Stimme klingt. Das erfasste laut DeepL, wer spricht, aber nicht wie. Eine feste Momentaufnahme kann einem Wechsel in Emotion, Betonung oder Tempo nicht folgen und auch keinen Vortrag wiedergeben, der den Worten widerspricht, etwa Sarkasmus.

Aure analysiert eingehende Sprache fortlaufend und nutzt dabei sowohl die übersetzten Wörter als auch das Original-Audio. DeepL nennt drei Probleme, die zusammen gelöst werden mussten. Echte Gespräche sind laut, das Modell muss Stimme und Prosodie also von Hintergrundgeräuschen, Echo und Verzerrungen trennen. Eine Stimme über Sprachgrenzen zu tragen, ohne Akzente zu übertreiben, ist schwieriger als innerhalb einer Sprache. Und es gibt wenig echte Daten derselben Person in mehreren Sprachen, auch weil DeepL Voice Transkripte und Übersetzungen von Meetings nicht dauerhaft speichert und sie am Ende einer Sitzung aus dem Speicher löscht. Aure muss sich deshalb in Echtzeit an jeden Sprecher anpassen, noch bevor ein Satz zu Ende ist.

Dafür kombiniert DeepL Trainingsverfahren, die Stimmidentität, Prosodie und gesprochenen Inhalt trennen, sodass jeder Teil für sich in eine neue Sprache übertragen werden kann. Reinforcement Learning verfeinert die Ausgabe auf Übersetzungsgenauigkeit und natürlich klingende Sprache.

## Wo es läuft

Aure greift automatisch und ohne Konfiguration in DeepL Voice for Online Meetings, DeepL Voice for In-Person Conversations und der DeepL API for Voice. Zunächst unterstützt es Englisch, Deutsch, Spanisch, Französisch, Italienisch, Japanisch, Portugiesisch und Koreanisch, weitere Sprachen sollen folgen. Andere Sprachen laufen weiter über die bestehenden Sprachmodelle von DeepL.

## Was noch offen ist

Die Beispiele von DeepL stammen aus dem Arbeitsalltag: eine Pause vor einer wichtigen Ankündigung, Nachdruck in einer Verhandlung, der Wechsel von ernst zu begeistert, wenn ein internationales Team gute Nachrichten bekommt. Wie zuverlässig Aure solche Momente überträgt, hat bisher niemand unabhängig geprüft. Die Angaben stammen vom Hersteller.

## Live translation that sounds like you

DeepL Voice already kept a speaker's own recognizable voice instead of a generic computer voice. Aure adds the changes in that voice during a conversation.

Im Training hat DeepL dem Modell beigebracht, drei Dinge getrennt zu behandeln: wessen Stimme es ist, wie sie sich in Melodie und Rhythmus bewegt, und die Wörter selbst. So können die Wörter die Sprache wechseln, während Stimme und Sprechweise bei der Person bleiben.

Schon vorher behielt DeepL Voice die eigene, wiedererkennbare Stimme eines Sprechers statt einer austauschbaren Computerstimme. Aure ergänzt nun die Veränderungen dieser Stimme im Gespräch.

## Wo es läuft

Aure ist automatisch aktiv, ohne Einrichtung: in DeepL Voice für Meetings in Programmen wie Microsoft Teams oder Zoom, für Gespräche vor Ort und für Entwickler über die DeepL API. Zum Start deckt es Englisch, Deutsch, Spanisch, Französisch, Italienisch, Japanisch, Portugiesisch und Koreanisch ab. Weitere Sprachen sollen folgen.

DeepL Voice speichert Transkripte und Übersetzungen von Meetings nicht dauerhaft. Die Daten werden gelöscht, wenn eine Sitzung endet.

## Was noch offen ist

All das ist bisher die Darstellung von DeepL. Einen Test von außen, wie gut Aure den Tonfall wirklich trifft, hat noch niemand veröffentlicht.

## Beyond voice preservation

On 11 November 2026 DeepL unveiled Aure, the model now powering DeepL Voice, its real-time speech translation product. DeepL calls it its most dynamic and lifelike voice AI model yet. Aure continuously adapts translated speech to shifts in tone, emotion, emphasis and pace.

It builds on DeepL's recent voice preservation launch, which rendered translations in the speaker's own recognizable voice instead of a generic synthetic one. That solved identity. Aure targets expression: how that voice changes over a conversation.

## Why the static sample failed

Previously, DeepL Voice generated an expressive voice from a static sample, using the opening moments of a conversation to fix how the translated voice should sound. In DeepL's words, that captured who was speaking, but not how. A fixed snapshot cannot track a later change in emotion, emphasis or pace, and it cannot convey delivery that contradicts the words, such as sarcasm.

Aure instead analyzes incoming speech continuously, conditioning delivery on both the translated words and the source audio.

## Three problems at once

DeepL describes three challenges it had to solve together. First, noise: the model must isolate voice identity and prosody from background noise, echo and audio distortion. Second, cross-lingual transfer: carrying a voice into another language without exaggerating accents or distorting how someone sounds. Third, data: DeepL has limited real-world recordings of the same speaker across languages, in part because DeepL Voice does not permanently store meeting transcripts or translations and deletes them from memory when a session ends. Aure therefore adapts to each speaker in real time, before a sentence is finished, and has to separate a speaker's stable characteristics from day-to-day variation such as fatigue, enthusiasm or stress.

The approach combines training techniques that disentangle voice identity, prosody and spoken content so each can be carried into the target language independently. Reinforcement learning then refines the output, trading off translation accuracy, speech quality and natural, accent-free speech.

## Deployment and caveats

Aure is applied automatically, with no configuration, across DeepL Voice for Online Meetings, DeepL Voice for In-Person Conversations and the DeepL API for Voice. Initial languages are English, German, Spanish, French, Italian, Japanese, Portuguese and Korean; others continue on DeepL's existing voice models.

DeepL names Pioneer Corporation, Aramark, Avendra International and Inetum as DeepL Voice customers. There is no independent benchmark of Aure's prosody transfer yet, and DeepL publishes no latency or quality figures in the announcement. The open question for any expressive system also applies here: a misread tone gets carried across with the same confidence as a correct one.

## Mehr als Stimmerhaltung

Am 11. November 2026 hat DeepL Aure vorgestellt, das Modell, auf dem DeepL Voice jetzt läuft, das Echtzeit-Übersetzungsprodukt für Sprache. DeepL nennt es sein bislang dynamischstes und lebensechtestes Voice-AI-Modell. Aure passt die übersetzte Sprache fortlaufend an Wechsel in Tonfall, Emotion, Betonung und Tempo an.

Es baut auf der kürzlich eingeführten Stimmerhaltung auf, die Übersetzungen in der eigenen, wiedererkennbaren Stimme des Sprechers ausgibt statt in einer generischen synthetischen. Damit war die Identität gelöst. Aure zielt auf den Ausdruck: wie sich diese Stimme im Gespräch verändert.

## Warum die feste Probe nicht reichte

Bisher erzeugte DeepL Voice eine ausdrucksstarke Stimme aus einer statischen Probe. Die ersten Momente eines Gesprächs legten fest, wie die übersetzte Stimme klingt. Das erfasste laut DeepL, wer spricht, aber nicht wie. Eine feste Momentaufnahme kann späteren Wechseln in Emotion, Betonung oder Tempo nicht folgen und keinen Vortrag wiedergeben, der den Worten widerspricht, etwa Sarkasmus.

Aure analysiert eingehende Sprache dagegen fortlaufend und richtet den Vortrag sowohl an den übersetzten Wörtern als auch am Original-Audio aus.

## Drei Probleme auf einmal

DeepL beschreibt drei Herausforderungen, die zusammen gelöst werden mussten. Erstens Lärm: Das Modell muss Stimmidentität und Prosodie von Hintergrundgeräuschen, Echo und Verzerrungen trennen. Zweitens der Sprachwechsel: Eine Stimme soll in eine andere Sprache wandern, ohne Akzente zu übertreiben oder den Klang zu verfälschen. Drittens Daten: DeepL hat wenig echte Aufnahmen derselben Person in mehreren Sprachen, auch weil DeepL Voice Transkripte und Übersetzungen von Meetings nicht dauerhaft speichert und sie zum Sitzungsende aus dem Speicher löscht. Aure passt sich deshalb in Echtzeit an jeden Sprecher an, noch bevor ein Satz endet, und muss stabile Merkmale einer Stimme von Tagesform wie Müdigkeit, Begeisterung oder Stress unterscheiden.

Der Ansatz kombiniert Trainingsverfahren, die Stimmidentität, Prosodie und gesprochenen Inhalt entkoppeln, sodass jeder Teil unabhängig in die Zielsprache übertragen werden kann. Reinforcement Learning verfeinert danach die Ausgabe und wägt Übersetzungsgenauigkeit, Sprachqualität und natürliche, akzentfreie Sprache gegeneinander ab.

## Einsatz und Vorbehalte

Aure greift automatisch und ohne Konfiguration in DeepL Voice for Online Meetings, DeepL Voice for In-Person Conversations und der DeepL API for Voice. Die ersten Sprachen sind Englisch, Deutsch, Spanisch, Französisch, Italienisch, Japanisch, Portugiesisch und Koreanisch, andere laufen weiter über die bestehenden Sprachmodelle.

Als Kunden von DeepL Voice nennt das Unternehmen Pioneer Corporation, Aramark, Avendra International und Inetum. Einen unabhängigen Benchmark für die Prosodie-Übertragung gibt es noch nicht, Latenz- oder Qualitätswerte nennt die Ankündigung nicht. Und es gilt, was für jedes ausdrucksstarke System gilt: Ein falsch gelesener Tonfall wird mit derselben Sicherheit übertragen wie ein richtiger.

headline: AI checks Signal's code

deepDiveMarkdown:
## DeepMind verifies the code, not just the design

Google DeepMind announced AlphaProof Code on 10 November 2026. In a blog post, Pushmeet Kohli and Swarat Chaudhuri write that researchers "guided AI agents to mathematically prove key security properties of the actual code underlying the Signal protocol," the technology behind private conversations in Signal, Google Messages and other apps.

Cryptographic protocols have been formally analyzed for decades, but most of that work stops at the design level. DeepMind's agents went further and proved that the compiled code meets the specified properties, for example keeping messages protected before and after a device is temporarily compromised. Real-world vulnerabilities, the post notes, often hide in the gap between design and implementation.

## Humans set the goals, agents write the proofs

AlphaProof Code splits the work the way a research team would. Researchers worked with a mix of models to translate Signal's security goals into formal specifications, and human experts reviewed every one. Agents powered by Gemini Carbon then produced the proofs: over six million lines of Lean, according to the blog, and about 6.5 million according to the accompanying paper. Lean's kernel checks every proof, and the agents flagged about one percent of the codebase for a second look by a human.

The whole campaign took four weeks. To test whether the system can tell correct code from buggy code, the team reintroduced two real, previously fixed bugs into an isolated copy of the code. In both cases it produced a machine-checked proof that the buggy version was insecure.

Signal's CTO Ehren Kret calls the use of agents to translate live code into valid Lean theorems "a major breakthrough."

## What the proofs leave out

The paper is more precise than the blog. It targets libsignal v0.105.4, compiled to AArch64 machine code, and is restricted to one-to-one sessions; group messaging is left for future work. The cryptographic primitives are assumed rather than proved, and side channels are out of scope. The paper also says the theorems do not rule out a known replay-based loss of forward secrecy.

That does not make the result small. But "Signal is verified" is a broader claim than either document makes.

## Open artifacts and bigger plans

DeepMind is open-sourcing the formal verification artifacts, and the Lean development is public. The lab sees the work as groundwork for securing other critical software, from medical device firmware to power grid software, and wants to pair formal verification with automated defense agents such as CodeMender. Scaling the technique, it says, still requires more research.

## From design proofs to machine code

Google DeepMind published AlphaProof Code on 10 November 2026, with a blog post by Pushmeet Kohli and Swarat Chaudhuri and a technical paper. The paper describes it as "a multi-agent AI framework for formal software specification and verification" and applies it to libsignal, the Signal protocol's reference implementation, "at the machine-code level."

Most protocol verification stops at the design. Here the theorems are stated over a formal semantics of user-mode AArch64 Linux written in Lean. The artifact is unmodified libsignal v0.105.4, linked into a small command-line harness and compiled with stock rustc. The paper calls the results "the first proofs connecting protocol-level security guarantees to the unmodified code of a widely used cryptographic protocol implementation." The blog goes further and calls it the first formal verification of such an implementation by any method.

## A trusted spec and untrusted provers

AlphaProof Code has three parts: a human-guided agent that writes Lean specifications, the AArch64 semantics, and a team of autonomous prover agents whose proofs count only if Lean's kernel accepts them against the approved specification. The blog says human experts reviewed every specification and that the provers were powered by Gemini Carbon.

The paper reports about 6.5 million lines of machine-checked proof code resting on about 26,000 lines of trusted specifications and AArch64 semantics. The blog adds that agents flagged roughly one percent of the codebase for human review. The properties are forward secrecy, authentication, post-compromise security and handshake secrecy for the PQXDH handshake and the Triple Ratchet, which combines the Double Ratchet with the Sparse Post-Quantum Ratchet. There are two independent arguments, one in the symbolic model and one in the computational model.

As a sanity check, the team reverse-applied two upstream bug fixes and recompiled. The resulting binaries violate the symbolic security theorems. According to the paper, the proof work was done by a team of five over four weeks.

## The boundaries of the theorems

The scope is one-to-one sessions; group messaging, sealed sender and server-side protocols are named as future work. Cryptographic primitives are hooked out to trusted contracts, idealized in the symbolic model and assumed hard in the computational one. Side channels and other secrets in memory are out of scope. The paper also states that the forward secrecy and post-compromise results do not rule out the replay-based loss of forward secrecy described by Cheval et al.

The theorems are only as strong as the trusted specification. A weaker attacker model in the statement means a weaker result, however many lines of proof sit on top.

## Open development, open questions

The Lean development is public, with a map from paper sections to the code. Signal's CTO Ehren Kret calls the translation of live code into valid Lean theorems "a major breakthrough." DeepMind wants to extend the approach to medical device firmware and power grid software and to pair it with defense agents such as CodeMender, while noting that scaling it needs more research.

For anyone reviewing critical code, the interesting part is the division of labor: humans own a comparatively small trusted specification, and machines carry the bulk of the proof.

Der Blog geht weiter und nennt es die erste formale Verifikation einer solchen Implementierung überhaupt.

## Vertraute Spezifikation, unvertraute Prover

AlphaProof Code besteht aus drei Teilen: einem von Menschen geführten Agent, der Lean-Spezifikationen schreibt, der AArch64-Semantik und einem Team autonomer Prover-Agents. Deren Beweise zählen nur, wenn Leans Kernel sie gegen die freigegebene Spezifikation akzeptiert. Laut Blog haben Fachleute jede Spezifikation geprüft, die Prover liefen auf Gemini Carbon.

Der Aufsatz nennt rund 6,5 Millionen Zeilen maschinell geprüften Beweiscode auf einer Basis von etwa 26.000 Zeilen vertrauter Spezifikation und AArch64-Semantik. Der Blog ergänzt, die Agents hätten rund ein Prozent des Codes für eine menschliche Prüfung markiert. Bewiesen sind Forward Secrecy, Authentifizierung, Post-Compromise Security und Handshake-Geheimhaltung für PQXDH und den Triple Ratchet, der den Double Ratchet mit dem Sparse Post-Quantum Ratchet kombiniert. Es gibt zwei unabhängige Argumente, eines im symbolischen und eines im komputationalen Modell.

Zur Gegenprobe machte das Team zwei Fehlerbehebungen aus dem Upstream rückgängig und kompilierte neu. Die so entstandenen Binaries verletzen die symbolischen Sicherheitstheoreme. Die Beweisarbeit erledigte laut Aufsatz ein Team von fünf Personen in vier Wochen.

## Wo die Theoreme enden

Der Umfang beschränkt sich auf Zweiergespräche. Gruppenchats, Sealed Sender und serverseitige Protokolle nennt der Aufsatz als künftige Arbeit. Kryptoprimitive sind über vertraute Verträge ausgelagert, im symbolischen Modell idealisiert, im komputationalen als schwer zu brechen vorausgesetzt. Seitenkanäle und andere Geheimnisse im Speicher sind ausgeklammert. Außerdem schließen die Ergebnisse zu Forward Secrecy und Post-Compromise Security den von Cheval et al. beschriebenen Replay-bedingten Verlust der Forward Secrecy nicht aus.

Die Theoreme sind nur so stark wie die vertraute Spezifikation. Ein schwächeres Angreifermodell in der Aussage bedeutet ein schwächeres Ergebnis, egal wie viele Zeilen Beweis darauf aufbauen.

## Offene Entwicklung, offene Fragen

Die Lean-Entwicklung ist öffentlich, samt einer Zuordnung von Abschnitten des Aufsatzes zum Code. Signals Technikchef Ehren Kret nennt die Übersetzung von laufendem Code in gültige Lean-Theoreme einen „großen Durchbruch“. DeepMind will den Ansatz auf Firmware medizinischer Geräte und Software für Stromnetze ausweiten und mit Abwehr-Agents wie CodeMender verbinden, räumt aber ein, dass die Skalierung weitere Forschung braucht.

Für alle, die kritischen Code prüfen, ist die Arbeitsteilung das Spannende: Menschen verantworten eine vergleichsweise kleine, vertraute Spezifikation, Maschinen tragen den Großteil der Beweislast.
